title: Nick Jonas Is on a US Podcast Telling Americans to Visit India and Watch His Wife's New Film. Priyanka Chopra's 'Varanasi' Might Be the Most Expensive Indian Film Ever Made.
excerpt: On the Smartless Podcast, Nick Jonas called Priyanka's return to Indian cinema 'a big, big deal,' joked she's '75 years old,' and praised Indian audiences as 'unlike anything I've ever seen.' The ₹1,300-crore SS Rajamouli epic releases April 2027.
body:
There's a moment in Nick Jonas's recent appearance on the Smartless Podcast — hosted by Jason Bateman, Sean Hayes, and Will Arnett — where he casually tells three of America's most famous comedians that his wife has made over 80 films. Then he pauses, deadpan: "She's 75 years old, Will."

It's a joke, obviously. Priyanka Chopra Jonas is 43. But it's also the kind of off-hand promotion that money can't buy — Nick Jonas, mid-tour with the Jonas Brothers, using one of the biggest podcasts in the US to hype his wife's return to Indian cinema.

## What Nick Said

The relevant exchange is worth quoting in full. After encouraging the hosts to visit India, Nick shared: "Priyanka has been shooting there. This movie by the director that did RRR was his last film. Big Indian kind of epic film and she's not done a movie there in about eight years. So it's a big, big deal… her return."

He went on to praise Indian audiences with the kind of genuine enthusiasm that feels unrehearsed: "The way in which the Indian audience reveres their film talent, their stars, is unlike anything I've ever seen before. And it's obviously an enormous audience, over a billion people in India. And then globally, the reach is so big."

For a podcast audience that mostly knows Nick Jonas as a pop star and Priyanka as "the actress from Quantico," this is a masterclass in cultural translation. He's not just promoting a film — he's contextualising Indian cinema for an American audience that's only now waking up to its scale.

## The Film: Varanasi

*Varanasi*, directed by SS Rajamouli (who needs no introduction after *Baahubali* and *RRR*), is shaping up to be one of the most ambitious Indian films ever attempted. The budget is reportedly between ₹1,000 and ₹1,300 crore — which, for context, would make it the most expensive Indian film in history, surpassing even *Ramayana*.

The plot follows the adventures of Rudhra as the ancient city of Varanasi faces the impending arrival of an asteroid. The narrative reportedly spans multiple timelines and continents — the kind of genre-blending, globe-trotting spectacle that Rajamouli has proven he can execute at a scale that rivals Hollywood.

Mahesh Babu leads the cast, with Prithviraj Sukumaran in a major role alongside Priyanka. The film is being shot across India (currently in Hyderabad), with reports of an Antarctica schedule still to come. The worldwide release is set for April 7, 2027.

## Mangoes in Hyderabad

Meanwhile, Priyanka is doing what anyone shooting in Hyderabad during late May should be doing: eating Himayat mangoes. Her Instagram story — a bowl of the prized fruit in her vanity van, captioned "Mango love" — is the kind of effortlessly relatable content that reminds you she's still, at heart, an Indian woman who knows her mango varieties.

It's also a small signal that the Hyderabad schedule is in full swing. Six months of shooting reportedly remain, which tracks with the April 2027 release date.

## Why NRIs Should Pay Attention

Priyanka Chopra's trajectory is the NRI entertainment story. Bollywood star, Miss World, Hollywood crossover, married to an American pop star, raising a daughter in Los Angeles — and now returning to Indian cinema not for a small comeback film, but for the biggest, most expensive project in the industry's history.

For diaspora audiences who've followed her career since *Krrish* and *Fashion*, this return carries genuine emotional weight. Priyanka didn't need to come back. She has a thriving Hollywood career (The Bluff, Citadel Season 2). The fact that she chose Rajamouli's most ambitious project — and that Rajamouli chose her — says something about where Indian cinema is headed.

And then there's Nick Jonas, casually telling 30 million Smartless listeners that Indian cinema produces "some of the best" content he's ever seen. That's not PR. That's a guy who married into the culture and actually gets it.

## The Numbers Game

If *Varanasi* delivers on its promise, it could be the film that definitively proves Indian cinema can compete with Hollywood at the global box office. *RRR* cracked the US market with a $15 million theatrical run. *Baahubali 2* did similar numbers. A Rajamouli film with Priyanka Chopra — an actress American audiences actually recognise — shooting for a simultaneous worldwide release in multiple languages, with a budget that rivals mid-tier Marvel films?

The math starts to look very different.

April 7, 2027. Mark it.
image_caption: Priyanka Chopra's return to Indian cinema with SS Rajamouli's Varanasi could redefine global box office expectations
nri_angle: Priyanka Chopra is the NRI entertainment story personified — an Indian actress who conquered Hollywood and is now returning to Indian cinema with the country's most ambitious filmmaker. Nick Jonas promoting Varanasi on a major US podcast is exactly the kind of cross-cultural bridge that diaspora audiences have been waiting for. Her return validates the idea that Indian cinema is now a global industry, not a regional one.
